PullRequest.Title: Private Marketplace extension blocking: add workbench UX and update gating
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- restore extension blocking metadata on the workbench model and refresh installed extensions when same-version blocking presence or origin changes
- prevent blocked extensions from auto-updating or being installed, disable the per-extension auto-update toggle, and set `extensionDisallowInstall`
- surface state-aware blocked status messaging: uninstalled extensions keep the installation-blocked explanation, while installed extensions explain that updates are blocked with policy/Marketplace attribution
- exclude blocked extensions from the extension search tool
- add focused coverage for metadata refresh, update/install gating, toggle state, status wording, and search filtering

## Stack

Depends on #333859. This PR is based on that branch, so it temporarily includes the platform commit; GitHub will narrow the diff to the workbench/UI commit after #333859 merges.

## Validation

- `scripts\test.bat` for `searchExtensionsTool.test.ts`, `extensionsWorkbenchService.test.ts`, and `extensionsActions.test.ts`
- targeted ESLint for all seven changed files
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`

---
🤖 *This pull request description was authored by GitHub Copilot CLI on behalf of @mcumming.*

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The before/after critical-path change is explicit in the diff, and the awaited method's target-platform, fallback Marketplace query, and metadata-write paths are directly traced. The exact delay varies with installed/page overlap and service latency, but the added wait and realistic incompatible-installed-extension trigger are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Marketplace network requests, extension-management IPC calls, and extension-profile filesystem writes
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Every first-page gallery search, subsequent page fetch, and direct extension lookup now waits for reconciliation on each configured local/remote/web extension server. If a page contains installed extensions whose returned versions are incompatible, each server performs one additional grouped getExtensions Marketplace request; UUID-less matches can also perform metadata lookups and sequential metadata writes.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased extension-search and paging latency, potentially up to an additional Marketplace request or remote-service timeout before results render.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: queryGallery/getPage/getExtensions invoked syncInstalledExtensionsWithGallery without awaiting it, so the pager or mapped gallery results were returned after the primary gallery query while compatibility reconciliation and metadata persistence continued off the result critical path.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added await makes query completion depend on Promise.allSettled across all extension servers. Each server unconditionally awaits getTargetPlatform, checks installed matches, can issue galleryService.getExtensions for incompatible matches, and can persist missing gallery metadata before resolving.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1480 changes `this.syncInstalledExtensionsWithGallery(pager.firstPage);` to `await this.syncInstalledExtensionsWithGallery(pager.firstPage);`; the same change is also made for page fetches and getExtensions, moving the existing asynchronous boundary work onto each caller's critical path.
Findings.Title: Keep gallery reconciliation off the search critical path
Findings.Impact: Opening or typing in the Extensions view, paging results, and extension-tool ID lookups can now pause for a second Marketplace round trip whenever a page includes an installed extension whose latest gallery version is not compatible with the current local or remote target; slow or unavailable remote services can delay the whole result as well.
Findings.Evidence: The changed line awaits syncInstalledExtensionsWithGallery. That method awaits all configured Extensions.syncInstalledExtensionsWithGallery calls (line 2222). Each call awaits getTargetPlatform (line 752), and incompatible installed matches are grouped into galleryService.getExtensions(... queryAllVersions: true) (lines 763-765), an additional network query. UUID-less installed matches then await updateMetadata inside the result loop (line 683), which can query the Marketplace for the local version (line 802) and persists through extension-management IPC/profile storage (line 805).
Findings.Recommendation: Refresh the blocking metadata needed by this PR synchronously/in memory before mapping the returned page, but leave compatibility resolution and metadata persistence off the query critical path as before (or split the method into a fast blocking-state refresh and a background reconciliation). Preserve ordering for the blocking-state update without awaiting unrelated target-platform, Marketplace fallback, or profile-write work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browse or search the Extensions view and fetch result pages
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing control-manifest read and primary Marketplace gallery query must complete. The diff additionally makes all installed-extension reconciliation complete before the first page or a later page is returned; target-platform resolution, compatible-version fallback, and metadata persistence are therefore newly on the rendering critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing query per requested page, plus the separate preferred-results work already used by some search modes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same primary query was awaited before results were returned.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing prerequisite for displaying gallery results.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve target platform for each configured extension-management server
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per configured server per reconciliation; IPC-backed clients cache the promise, so only cold calls cross the channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Reconciliation invoked this after queryGallery had started returning results, without delaying the pager.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Newly awaited before every gallery page is returned; a cold or slow remote server can hold the whole page.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch all compatible versions for installed matches whose page version is incompatible
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one grouped getExtensions request per configured server per page when one or more installed matches are incompatible.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same fallback request ran in background reconciliation and did not block returning gallery results.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Newly adds a sequential Marketplace round trip before the page can render.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist gallery identifiers and publisher metadata for legacy UUID-less installed extensions, then rescan
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One write/rescan per UUID-less installed match, awaited serially within each server; an additional exact-version Marketplace lookup occurs when versions differ.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Metadata repair ran after the result was returned.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Newly blocks gallery result delivery on cold legacy metadata repair.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A gallery page (typically tens of extensions), its overlap with installed extensions, and up to three configured local/remote/web extension-management servers. Effective Marketplace fallback cardinality is grouped to at most one request per server per page, not one per extension.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Local, remote, and web server reconciliation runs in parallel via Promise.allSettled. Within each server, compatibility checks run concurrently, one fallback gallery lookup is grouped, and UUID-less metadata updates are awaited serially in the result loop. Independent searches are not coalesced here.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The IPC extension-management client caches its target-platform promise after the first call. Compatibility fallback queries are not shown to be cached or coalesced. Metadata persistence is mainly a cold/legacy path because a successful write supplies the missing UUID; warm searches still await reconciliation even if it resolves in memory.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff explicitly adds awaits, and all transitive boundaries and grouping behavior are visible in the traced methods.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact delay depends on installed-result overlap, compatibility, remote configuration, and service latency; warm target-platform caches and repaired metadata reduce frequency. A second network round trip for an incompatible installed extension remains a realistic trigger.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium latency regression; submitted a finding anchored to the first-page await, which also covers identical waits added for page fetches and direct lookups.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve explicit extension IDs, including the extension search tool
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The primary getExtensions Marketplace request was already required. The diff now also awaits installed-extension reconciliation before returning IDs to the caller; the tool's new blocked-extension filter itself is an in-memory linear pass.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Grouped for the requested ID collection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing prerequisite for returning extension models.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compatible-version fallback during newly awaited reconciliation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one grouped fallback per configured extension server when an installed match is incompatible.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Reconciliation was launched without awaiting it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Newly blocks direct lookup and tool completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of requested IDs and overlap with installed extensions; the tool commonly handles a small explicit list, while other callers can request larger update or extension-description sets.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: ID lookup is grouped by gallery service. Reconciliation is parallel across extension servers but can perform one grouped compatible-version fallback per server; the search tool's keyword queries remain sequential as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Same target-platform promise cache and one-time UUID metadata repair as gallery browsing. No new cache is introduced by the blocked filter.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the changed wait and fallback path; lower only for prevalence of incompatible installed IDs in tool requests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Explicit tool ID lists are usually small, but an installed incompatible ID still adds a full network round trip. Other getExtensions callers may provide larger collections.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the submitted critical-path reconciliation finding; the added filtering condition is not independently expensive.

Scenarios.Scenario: Select a prior unblocked version when the latest gallery version is blocked
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A latest-only Marketplace query completes first. If blocking makes the returned latest version invalid, queryGalleryExtensions performs one grouped IncludeVersions query and waits for it before returning the prior unblocked version or no result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Latest-only Marketplace query followed by grouped IncludeVersions fallback
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One primary query plus at most one grouped secondary query for all affected IDs in that request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A blocked marker did not invalidate the latest version, so this specific trigger did not cause the all-versions fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The secondary request adds a round trip before displaying an older unblocked version.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Whether at least one extension in the requested page has a blocked latest/version selection; all affected extension IDs are grouped into one secondary request regardless of count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The secondary all-versions request is serialized after the latest-only response and grouped across all affected IDs on the page.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No query-result cache or negative cache is evident in the reviewed path, so repeated affected searches can repeat the grouped fallback. The fallback only occurs when the initial latest-version response cannot produce a valid result.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: tests explicitly assert two POSTs and the needAllVersions grouping is direct. User-scale magnitude is uncertain.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Blocked latest versions should be uncommon in public results, though tenant policy could increase prevalence. The service contract does not expose a narrower way in this code to retrieve the prior unblocked version from a latest-only response.
Scenarios.Verdict: Not separately reported: the extra request is bounded to one grouped fallback and is necessary in the current API path to preserve the PR's explicit behavior of selecting an older unblocked version.

Scenarios.Scenario: Install, update, auto-update, and settings-sync handling of blocked extensions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Blocking checks are in-memory and occur before target-platform validation or install/download work. Auto-update selection skips blocked models locally. Sync only classifies the newly emitted NotAllowed error as skippable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: VSIX acquisition and gallery compatibility calls on install/update paths
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing per installation/update behavior; blocked candidates now stop before acquisition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Blocked metadata was not checked, so normal install validation and acquisition could proceed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The diff avoids rather than adds these operations for blocked extensions.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of install/update candidates or synchronized extensions; each candidate receives a constant-time property/origin check.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No changed concurrency mechanism. Existing install/update batching remains intact; blocked items are removed before expensive acquisition.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Blocking state arrives with gallery objects and is not separately cached. No new retained collection or negative-cache behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of blocked candidates varies by policy, but the changed mechanism short-circuits expensive work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; these paths reduce work for blocked extensions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render extension actions and blocked status messaging
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Context-menu state, auto-update toggle state, and status wording are computed from already-present blocking metadata. The blocked status branch returns before the unsigned-extension manifest check.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Extension-gallery manifest lookup for unsigned status
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing lookup for applicable uninstalled unsigned extensions; blocked extensions now return before it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Blocked metadata had no early status branch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No new boundary; blocked status can avoid an existing manifest lookup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One constant-time property check per rendered/recomputed extension action or menu item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous in-memory checks only; no new queue, listener, or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or retained state is added; MarkdownString allocation is per status computation and bounded.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Status recomputation frequency depends on UI activity, but added work is constant and trivial.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 14 changed files. One concrete regression was submitted: awaiting full installed-extension reconciliation moves grouped Marketplace fallback, extension-management IPC, and legacy metadata writes onto gallery search/page/direct-lookup critical paths. Blocked-version fallback, install/update gating, sync handling, search filtering, and UI status paths were separately assessed without additional reportable issues.
